notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

New systems: Master System and Sega CD tabs, both on Genesis Plus GX. Sega CD games go in as .chd, .cue and .bin, or .iso, and need the Sega CD BIOS for their region, uploaded on the web page under Files, BIOS. A game that is missing it names the file it needs.

Pokemon: Pokemon XD: Gale of Darkness is a tile of its own, built on the console from your own disc, as Pokemon Colosseum is. Colosseum builds version 0.5.0, and both games have new options on their game page, under Performance settings: Gen 4 battle rules (XD makes them from your Colosseum disc), a randomizer with an optional seed, texture packs and a Game Boy Advance save for trades, the last two added through the game's Files window on the web page. Press Build the update for Colosseum; your save carries over.

DS: melonDS DS is a new engine for DS games, picked per game under Performance settings, Engine. It has RetroAchievements and save states, with touch, the lid and screen swap from the pause menu. melonDS also has its own screen layout per game, hybrid included.

PokeDaisy: a new engine for Pokemon games on Game Boy, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance and DS, picked per game. It shows a live companion with your party, the Pokedex, a map and a guide. It downloads from the PokeDaisy project the first time a game starts with it; without the internet the game starts on its usual engine. Your in-game save moves across; save states do not. Based on PokeDaisy by Lidor Itzhari - https://github.com/lidor30/pokedaisy

Ports: a port built on the console has a Build row on its game page, with its progress, so no web page is needed. Sly, Pokemon Colosseum and Black Ops II have an Uninstall button on the web page, and your saves stay.

PC games: a single .exe can be added as the game itself; the web page asks whether it is the game or its installer.

Look and feel: Settings opens on its sections as tiles. Each game's page shows its console's logo over the box, and Settings, Look and feel can theme the header and tabs in the selected console's logo and colors. Search has one row for the sort, the console and a random game, which spins a reel of covers.

Wii and Wii U: a Wii game's page has Motion source; Tilt the console uses the Switch's own motion sensor for Wii Remote 1 in handheld. Wii pointer speed is a slider from 70 to 150 percent, a Wii game's Rumble and pointer rows are under Controller options, and the hotkeys can shake the Wii Remote and recenter the pointer. Settings, Controllers has Set dead zone by hand. The web page's Saves tab takes your Wii U Mii file, and a Wii U game's page can download its shader cache.

Fixes: "Updated to" shows once the update has fully finished. The web page's Replace files prompt no longer opens behind the file browser. A PC game whose program is missing from its folder says so.

Not yet tried: a real Master System or Sega CD game, Pokemon XD past its title, Colosseum's options in a battle or a new game, an achievement unlocked on melonDS DS, the Wii hotkeys in a game, and docked play for most of the above. Reports welcome.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
